reading.body:
Bryan Steil's AI record is a funding record more than a legislative one: five AI company PACs gave his committee $16,000 across 2025 and 2026, while his AI bills are narrower than that donor list.

The pattern is concentration. Microsoft's PAC gave three times, Google's twice, Amazon's twice, Meta's twice, for $16,000 total between March 2025 and August 2026. The legislative side is thinner: one sponsored resolution on AI in financial services and housing, one cosponsored bill on AI innovation in financial services, and four recorded yea votes on bills the data does not describe. The two financial services items are the only ones whose subject matter is stated.

For AI specifically, this is the money side of the compute buildout's political footprint. Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta are the four companies whose data center and power demand drive the grid constraint, and their PACs are the ones appearing here. What the data does not show is any causal link between the contributions and the votes, and the page says so directly. It also does not say what H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, or S. 146 do, so the votes cannot be read as AI policy positions. The record covers one member's filings and votes, not the wider pattern.
